snippets.label: Route definition with typed state
snippets.why_it_matters: Axum's type-safe routing extracts path params and state at compile time — zero runtime panics from wrong types

snippets.label: Async background job (fire-and-forget)
snippets.why_it_matters: tokio::task::spawn gives Rust true async fire-and-forget without blocking the response — no threads wasted

snippets.label: Validation with derive macros
snippets.snippet:
#[derive(Debug, Deserialize, Validate)]
struct CreateUserRequest {
    #[validate(length(min = 1, max = 100))]
    name: String,
    #[validate(email)]
    email: String,
}
snippets.why_it_matters: Compile-time validation rules via derive macros — no runtime reflection, no hidden cost

snippets.label: sqlx typed query with connection pool
snippets.snippet:
let user = sqlx::query_as::<_, User>(
    "INSERT INTO users (name, email) VALUES ($1, $2) RETURNING id, name, email, created_at",
)
.bind(&payload.name)
.bind(&payload.email)
.fetch_one(&state.pool)
.await
snippets.why_it_matters: sqlx maps query results directly to structs at compile time — no ORM overhead, no reflection

snippets.why_it_matters: Fiber uses fasthttp under the hood — zero-allocation request handling that bypasses net/http overhead entirely

snippets.label: Goroutine fire-and-forget background job
snippets.why_it_matters: Go goroutines are ~2KB stack — launching thousands for background work costs almost nothing

snippets.label: pgxpool connection pool config
snippets.snippet:
config, err := pgxpool.ParseConfig(dbURL)
config.MinConns = 5
config.MaxConns = 20
pool, err := pgxpool.NewWithConfig(context.Background(), config)
snippets.why_it_matters: pgxpool is the fastest Go Postgres driver — binary protocol, prepared statements, and zero-copy reads

snippets.label: Minimal API route definition
snippets.why_it_matters: ASP.NET Minimal API cuts 90% of boilerplate vs MVC. Route parameters are parsed and typed automatically.

snippets.label: async/await background job
snippets.snippet:
_ = Task.Run(() =>
    Console.WriteLine($"NOTIFY: email sent to {user.Email} at {DateTime.UtcNow:O}"));
snippets.why_it_matters: Task.Run fire-and-forget — same pattern as other stacks but GC must track these tasks
